utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can fully follow the proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated and good afternoon to you. Appearances Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of the Prosecution, Joanne Richardson, counsel Gramsci Di Fazio, and our case manager, Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm Vasvija Vidovic, appearing for Mr. Oric, together with Mr. John Jones. Joining us here today are our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good afternoon to you. Can we proceed with the cross-examination of the witness? Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, just as a matter of organisation for this afternoon. If Madam Vidovic could give us even a rough estimation of how long, I can let people know when to bring the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe I will take two and a half hours. As always, however, I will do my best to keep it as brief as possible, depending on the witness's answers, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My suggestion to you, having some experience in -- I think an abundance of experience, I would have your next witness present here just before the next break. In other words, you should have him here in about an hour and a half's time. MR. DI FAZIO: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you. You may remain seated, and I will -- because I need to explain to the witness what's going to happen. And then, obviously, because I know from -- again from experience, how sometimes inconvenient it is for either Prosecution or the Defence when you are dealing with a witness to stop halfway and then continue two days later. So you choose the time, and the subject. Because I don't know whether you would be able to finish with this witness today. So if you are not in a position with this witness, with the next witness obviously, then you choose the subjects and the time when you would like to stop. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand completely. I'll certainly make my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- whether you will find us cooperative because this is -- anyone who's got trial experience knows exactly what I'm talking about. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll attend to that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Filipovic, good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to continue and finish with your testimony today. May I just remind you for the record that you are still under oath; in other words, you're still testifying on the basis of the solemn declaration that you entered yesterday. You understand that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. And Madam Vidovic now will start with her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you were a member of the Serbian Democratic Party, which I will from now on refer to as the SDS, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this area, throughout 1991 and 1992, the SDS was very active, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the president, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry. I had hoped that everything would go fine today so we proceed as efficiently as we could, but I see that the script, transcript on my monitor is not scrolling. So there seems to be something wrong. One moment until we fix this. I don't know whether on yours it is scrolling, but on mine it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] The same problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Let me just check on the other one. No, no. Sorry about this, Madam Vidovic. Do we need to stay in here or is it something that can be solved shortly or do we need to retire and come again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will probably have to repeat my initial questions. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we can see my first two questions in the transcript here. Yes. Both the questions and the answers have been recorded. Therefore, if that's all right, I would just like to resume my questioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic - Sikiric and Bjelovac - did it have more than 40 members of the SDS at the time? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, as in I don't know; or no, it didn't have?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to place the following document on the ELMO. It's an excerpt from the minutes of a meeting of the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bratunac, 1991, 1992, and 1993. Witness, can you please look at page 00835911 of the B/C/S version. The page is 03020609 of the English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, can you please have a look now. Look at number 9. Do you see the name Milenko Mirovic there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were close with this person, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. Throughout 1991, 1992, and 1993, Mr. Milenko Mirovic, also known as Miga [phoen], from Bjelovac, was a deputy in the Serbian Assembly of Bratunac, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not something that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document not appear to show that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Have you seen the title of this document? Members of the Assembly. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours. I'm now receiving French interpretation. I'm receiving French interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We all think very highly of you, Mr. Oric. So I think we need to find a solution to that. Are you receiving interpretation in B/C/S now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am, Your Honours. It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sometimes it happens, Mr. Oric. Sometimes it happens. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I thought that -- well --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, can you please look at the title of this document, minutes, members of the Serbian Assembly.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the fact that Mr. Mirovic was a deputy for the Bjelovac area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Be that as it may, you were close, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and we still are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Alongside with other members of the SDS from Bjelovac and Sikiric, he implemented the policies created by the SDS leadership in the area prior to the beginning of the war and at the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The SDS was preparing the Serbs in the area for the war long before the war began; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document that we have shown the witness, can it please be assigned a number as an exhibit, the document that he commented upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, Judge Eser has a question, and this will be assigned a number as Defence Exhibit D?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 98, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 98. Thank you. Yes, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, I would have two questions. The English translation reads Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bratunac. Now, does it mean it's identical with the SDS or is it something else? My question one. Question two: It speaks of Assembly Men of the Serbian Assembly and minutes for the years 1991, 1992, and 1993. Does this indicate that these people mentioned here have been members all these years or may they have been some time within these years, which would make it possible that somebody has been member in 1991, but not any more in 1993, or the other way around? So how is it -- is this to be interpreted?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have submitted the original of the document for translation. This is a very long document, in its entirety. On the title-page, it has a title "Minutes 1991, 1992, 1993." However, this is a translation as the document has been translated. That's all I can say. The translation is what it is. Instead of being translated separately, on a separate page, what happens is that the title-page starts running on the first page and reads "Minutes from 1991, 1992, and 1993." However, the document itself speaks about who the board members were of the Serbian Assembly, or deputy men, in 1991, 1992, and 1993. In our system, back at home, usually deputies are elected for a four-year term, and these were the Assembly men who were in the Serbian Assembly at the time. That is all I can give you. This is the document that we received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In addition, as a follow-up to your question, because I think it has only been partly and very partly answered. I notice that the document that you have submitted, and in the answer that you have given to Judge Eser, you have not answered the question that was put to you whether the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bratunac is the same as the SDS of Bratunac. And the other thing I wanted to note is that looking at the English translation and the previous two pages, forming part of this exhibit, and knowing a little bit of your language, I see that, while we have ERN 9 -- 5911 here and 5910, we do not have 5909, in which seems to be a specific reference to the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bratunac. That is missing from the original. Because this page does not say that. And the next page does not say that either. And the third page -- and the second page that you have in your language, apart from the Bratunac, in the first line, minutes here, in the first line, does not say the Serbian Municipal Assembly, but it just says "assemblymen of the Serbian Assembly." So your answer -- I would like an answer, basically, as to whether you -- whether the Serbian Municipal Assembly and SDS to you mean the same thing. I know the answer, but it's a question that has been put to you, not to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the Bosnian or Serbian original, under the title "Minutes," it says "deputies to the Serb Assembly" or "assemblymen," and this is an official translation, Assembly men or deputies. That's just under the title which says "Minutes." It says "assemblymen of the Serb Assembly." As far as I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have 5909. This is basically what I'm saying. We have 590 -- and it's in 5909 that you have the title of "the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bratunac."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 59 -- Your Honours, the page 590 -- yes. Yes. However, Your Honours, in our copy it is a black page. I will try to ask my colleagues from the OTP to give us a better copy. In our copy, the page is black. However, I believe this document to be perfectly clear and obvious, and the gist of my question went to Mr. Mirovic. The question was whether he was a deputy in the Serb Assembly on behalf of the Bjelovac area. The answer was that the witness didn't know, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my only comment with respect to this document is that with all due respect to Madam Vidovic's knowledge of the political system in Bosnia, I think it's still unclear that this is a document from the SDS. If this is the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bratunac, that's what it is. I don't know if there are more than one parties with respect to the Serb -- whether or not the Serbs had more than one political party. It's still unclear that this is in fact from the SDS. And then with respect to what Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have no indication so far that it is from the SDS, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what I have an indication of is, and it's only in the English page, not in the Serbian -- not in the B/C/S text. In the B/C/S -- in the English text, which consists of one paper, allegedly or supposedly reproducing the gist of three pages in B/C/S, we only have two corresponding pages. We don't have 5909, which is the only one of the three that specifically mention the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. And my objection, my second objection, would be to exactly that, that this page is missing. The Prosecution can look into whether or not this is also a blank page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know, but if it's blank, how can it be translated into English?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the Defence is claiming that it is blank and that they received this document from us. If that's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I haven't seen 5909. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we received this document, together with the SDS-related documents. It was disclosed to us by the OTP as part of the set of documents related to the SDS. There is a black page with the SDS sign, and that's all that can be seen on that particular page. Please accept my apologies for not submitting this page. We will be submitting the page in due course. But we received these documents as part of the SDS set from the OTP. If this is a problem, I can simply withdraw this document and use it in some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not a problem, but I have to be fair with Judge Eser. I have been here long enough to at least have a clear idea of what happened over the years during the conflict. But Judge Eser hasn't had that fortune or misfortune that I have had. And his question is a very pertinent one, and I can't answer it, because I have -- I am a trained lawyer and a trained judge, and I will only take into consideration in this case what emerges in this case, not what I know from other cases and from my own personal knowledge. So please do answer the question that Judge Eser put to you: Does the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bratunac mean the SDS or not? Or is it something different?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I answer the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can tell him privately what I think, but that doesn't count.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Bratunac consisted mainly of SDS members, and can we please have the witness confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The municipality of Bratunac Assembly did not merely consist of the SDS. In Bratunac there were two political parties, as in most other areas. The first one was Dear Allah, and the other one was the SDS. And the SDS, as has been maliciously underlined by some, was supposed to be some sort of democratic party.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, we're not talking about the Assembly of the Bratunac municipality, but rather the Serbian Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We're talking about the Assembly of the Serbian Democratic Party, in as far as I understand

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that there were no SDS members in that Serbian Assembly?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And you, in turn, agree that there were no Serbs in the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because you are firing questions and answers at each other without the usual pause that I have recommended and which causes so many problems to the interpreters, et cetera. And what I have here is a confusion, a total confusion. Let's go through it again - sorry - bit by bit. There was a question: Do you agree with me that there were no SDS members in that Serbian municipality? How can you speak of there not being any SDS members in the Serbian municipalities? So there's either a mistake in interpretation here or a mistake in the question, or I am getting confused. But I don't think I am getting confused. I normally don't. So -- but then there is the question, and you, in turn, agree -- the answer: "And you, in turn, agree that there were no Serbs in the SDS. How can anyone agree that there were no Serbs in the SDS and how can anyone agree that there were no SDS members in the Serbian Democratic -- in the Serbian Assembly? Let's start from here: Was there a municipality of Bratunac, not a Serbian municipality of Bratunac, a municipality of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there was a municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was it there in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was it there in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The entire year of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Until the war -- when did the war break out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] April or early May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what happened then in April or early May? What happened to this municipality, Municipal Assembly of Bratunac, when the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what was going on there. I didn't have any information about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did you first hear of a Serbian municipality of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But did you ever hear of a Serbian municipality of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard about the municipality of Bratunac, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you heard about the municipality of Bratunac, but you never heard about the Serbian municipality of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And how was the composition of the municipality of Bratunac? Was it representative of all the political parties, that is, the Serbs, the Muslims, the Bosniaks, and also the Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Until it lasted. You told me that until the war broke out, there was such a thing as the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and everyone was represented. It was the SDA and SDA party delegates who made up the Assembly, and the president of the municipality was a candidate of the SDA party. He came into power in 1991, and his name was Dubicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, look at the usher, please. Could the witness be shown the same document that he was referred to by Madam Vidovic. Look at the list of those Assembly men, 31 of them. Do you know those persons? Do you know the majority of them? Or do you know only a few of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You know them. Are they Serbs? Are they Croats? Are they Muslims? Or is that list composed of mixed ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So do you think that if this list consists of entirely of Serbian Assembly men, do you think that this is the list of the municipality of Bratunac or is it a list of a separate municipality, precisely called "the Serbian Municipality of Bratunac"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't say here. One thing, there is a party assembly, and the party had such a list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I will not pursue with it any further, because I think I have done enough to enable you also to give an answer. But there is an historical explanation to all this. So I'm not going into it, because it's a question of evidence. So either the evidence is brought forward or it isn't. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, please listen to my questions carefully and respond to what I ask. I may ask you about the SDA and the Muslims, and I may not. But please focus on my questions. I do not wish to enter into a polemic with you; I'm just trying to do my job. Please, Witness -- in fact, I'm asking the usher now to show the witness another document. Witness, please look at this document. It's a document of the Bratunac Brigade, 00656813. It's a certificate signed by Pero Petrovic, the company commander. Please look at the certificate, confirming that Milenko Ivanovic was mobilised on the 25th of March, 1992 into the TO Bjelovac and was there until the 28th of August, 1992. Mr. Filipovic, do you know Milenko Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I'll ask you something else. It's correct that the SDS mobilised the Serb population in the area as early as late March 1992, that is, before the general mobilisation of the Serbian population was announced by regular bodies, such as the Presidency; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I see here is a certificate. This is not a draft note.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is: Do you have any knowledge about the mobilisation of the Serbian population on the 25th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I move that this document be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document is being assigned Exhibit number D99.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the usher again to put on the ELMO document D37, a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the document. This is an order on the forming of staffs of the Territorial Defence of the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality of Bratunac, and it's dated 12th April 1992. I will quote number 1: "The TO of the Serbian Municipality shall take over all defence tasks in the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Bratunac." 2: "The TO of the Serbian Municipality comprises the following: Municipal Territorial Defence headquarters with headquarter support units, TO detachment, a company formation, local commune units," and so on. Mr. Filipovic, I will now put a question to you. As a member of the SDS, you will know that at that time, the SDS implemented its policy through crisis staffs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have anything to do with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- the correct answer to the question that was put to you. The question that was put to you is not whether you had anything to do with the crisis staffs set up by the SDS. The question was whether, as a member of the SDS, you knew that at the time the SDS implemented its policy through crisis staffs. We're talking during the conflict. No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the crisis staffs organised the local Serb population into Territorial Defence units?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about a crisis staff in my village, and as for the municipality of Bratunac, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, Mr. Filipovic, that the SDS was armed on a large scale by the JNA; they armed the local Serb population just before the outbreak of the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Filipovic. I'll move on. I will now show you a map of the Bjelovac area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... going to do with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I apologise. I think this has already been tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, it has a number. I just wanted to make sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, I will show you a map of Bjelovac and the surrounding area, and I will ask you to look at the places that I have highlighted in yellow, in order to make it easier for you to orient yourself on this map. This is a map of the Bjelovac area, and it's part of a map created by the military geographical institute. It was printed in 1971. Mr. Filipovic, please look at it, and can you please use the pointer to indicate and circle with a pencil the places I read out. Can you show us the area of Rakovac, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Pobrdje.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zaluzje?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Biljaca?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sikiric, and finally Sase. Could you please give the witness a pen so that he can circle these places and put his initials on the map, because we intend to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a need for that? I will just put on the record that the Trial Chamber could follow the witness confirming the position or the location of the villages or towns indicated to him by Madam Vidovic on the map, which is going to be given the exhibit number D100. And all these villages are highlighted in yellow on the said exhibit. Yes, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a question to the witness. Now, if you could look at the map. You see, at least in the version we have, that some places like Voljevica, Zaluzje, and Bjelovac are written in a horizontal way, whereas, what is it, Rakovac is written in a different way. Now, is Rakovac a village or is it a valley or a mountain? What is the difference between places like Bjelovac and Rakovac? Same type of village or municipality or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, on the map shown to us by the Prosecutor, we saw Sikiric written in the same way. This is the area of the village of Rakovac, and I ask that the witness correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Rakovac is a village, is it not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a kind of suburb of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's a village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I go on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's still no answer to Judge Eser's questions. Why is Bjelovac the only name or the only village that appears in italics and not in normal script? Is there an explanation for it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really have no explanation for this. All I know is that this is an official map published by the military geographical institute for the Zvornik area, and we have the original of this map, which I can show Your Honours. But I have no answer to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: May I have just another question. I must say for me still sometimes a little bit difficult to distinguish between villages and towns and municipalities. Now, yesterday we learned that the witness insisted he lived in Loznica and not in Bjelovac. Now, here Loznica is even written in a straighter script than Bjelovac. Now, what is the relationship between Bjelovac and Loznica? Is it Loznica part of Bjelovac? And if so, again, what is Bjelovac comprising? What is the relationship to Rakovac up there?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may the witness respond to this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can answer this question. I didn't know that we were partly in Serbia, because half the name is across the River Drina. Bjelovac is not a village. Loznica is a village. Bjelovac consists of six areas that together make up a local commune, and the land register says that Bjelovac -- well, Bjelovac doesn't actually exist. Loznica is a village, but Bjelovac consists of six areas, and as far as I can tell from this map, half the village is in Serbia, because it's across the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a map of the military geographical institute of the former Yugoslavia. It's only the letters that cross the border or the River Drina, not the marking of the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not even the letters should cross the Drina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed, because now we end up trying the military cartographers. Next question, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can I have the usher's assistance, please, to place on the ELMO an excerpt from the Bratunac Brigade documents, salaries for May 1992, prior to which, Witness, I would like to ask you to answer the following question:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the distance between Rakovac and Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same as Bratunac, about seven kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the previous document is being marked D100.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can Madam Usher please place the page 01320211 on the ELMO. This is a list of salaries for the month of May. If you could turn the page, please. The Rakovac list, 1st Platoon, this is the English version. Can you please just place the B/C/S. The B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, please have a good look. Look at this page closely. I asked you about the arming of the local Serb population a while ago. This is a list from the financial records dated May 1992. You see a number of names here. Can you please look with particular attention at the column which says "weapons." In connection with that, do you know, Mr. Filipovic, that PAP is a kind of rifle?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that PM stands for machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, can you please look at number 15. Stojadin Milovanovic, PM-72 is the sign.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this person?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that there is a weapon attached to his name, a 72 machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did say yes, didn't you? Did I get that correctly? Fair enough. Can you please now turn to page 01320213. It's a list for the 2nd Platoon, also showing -- please, if you could have a look, also showing a column entitled "weapons." Do you agree, Mr. Filipovic, that Rakovac is a small village? You said the distance from Bjelovac was seven kilometres, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven kilometres, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this not appear to mean that as early as May 1992, these people had been armed with different kinds of rifles, the PAP semi-automatic, automatic rifles, AP -- can you please just allow me to finish my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're going too fast, both of you. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Many of these had machine-guns too, didn't they? However, what I'm talking about now is this specific list of persons in relation to Rakovac, the one that you've just looked at.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that this document be assigned a number as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will be document -- Defence Exhibit D101. Next.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that many different TO units were set up and active in and around Bjelovac from May 1992 onwards?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know about the defence of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have Madam Usher's assistance, please, to place a different Bratunac document on the ELMO. The number is -- the number is 01320266. It's a list for the payment of salaries, May 1992. In the brackets, "(different TO units)."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please have a close look. At number 1 we can see Veso Simic, Rakovac, 50.000. Number 2, Zoran Simic, Bjelovac, again 50.000. And so on and so forth. Do you know any of these persons? Do you know Mr. Zoran Simic, for example?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in this period of time he was a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Mr. Filipovic, is it not true that in May 1992, units of the Territorial Defence were in fact so well organised that they were even receiving salaries, including Bjelovac and Rakovac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document please be assigned number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will be Defence Exhibit D102.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Usher, can you please place on the ELMO a Bratunac Brigade document, and the number is 01320174. This is a list of salaries for May 1992. The title is "List of soldiers of the 120-millimetre mortar platoon."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please have a look, sir. Mr. Filipovic, a while ago I asked you to show us Pobrdje on the map, and you obliged. You remember that, don't you? It's further down from Rakovac. Can you please now look at the first five names on this list. Savo Lukic, Pobrdje; Dragan Ostojic, also Pobrdje; Radivoje Prisic, again Pobrdje; Dragan Neskovic, Pobrdje; Zoran Prodanovic, Pobrdje. Mr. Filipovic, the first five persons on this list in relation to the 120-millimetre mortar platoon are all from Pobrdje.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what the document says. Do you know any of those persons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I then ask you something else now. 120-millimetre mortars are classified as heavy artillery, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it's some sort of a weapon, but I'm not sure about the type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do agree these are no rifles, no machine-guns; we're talking about heavy artillery here, right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were not shelling Serb villages, were they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea about that specific date.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I draw your attention to the fact that this document has a page of salaries in relation to May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, Witness, can you please answer my question. Were they shelling Muslim villages, in as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that. The distance is seven kilometres, after all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that this list of salaries for May 1992, the list of 120-millimetre mortar platoons, be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document will receive the documentation number D103.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will now show D82, a Defence exhibit. This is a census of Bosnia-Herzegovina in relation to Bratunac. I'm going to base my questions to the witness on that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, is it not true that Voljevica, before the war, had a total of 1.379 inhabitants and the number of Bosniaks was 375? In other words, was that not an exclusively Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a statistician, madam. How on earth should I know how many inhabitants there were?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, I'm not here to argue with you. Please, if you can't answer my question, just say no.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, it didn't have?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it had or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. May we just have a correction on the transcript. I said 1379, and the number of Bosniaks, 1375.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree that Zaluzje had 624 inhabitants and 621 of them were Bosniaks? Do you not agree that Zaluzje was predominantly Muslim?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not correct that Biljaca, the place that you showed us on the map, had 655 inhabitants, 622 of them Bosniaks, which means that it was a predominantly Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not correct that Sikiric had 442 inhabitants, 240 of them Bosniaks? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, Bjelovac had 290 inhabitants, 231 were Serbs and 59 were Bosniaks, and I'm referring to the local commune of Bjelovac. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Loznica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, not Loznica. I mean Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I still -- I'm really confused. You are insisting that you wanted to know the inhabitants of Bjelovac. We have heard that Bjelovac consisted of different village, that Bjelovac was not a village as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She said the commune.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: The commune. Comprising which villages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All the villages, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm presenting data established by the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina when carrying out the census of the village of Bjelovac. I suppose the authorities had in mind exactly what Bjelovac referred to, what it covered. I'm not sure whether the hamlets were included or not, but my reference was to our document, our Defence Exhibit D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But wait. Wait a minute. Your question was: Finally, Bjelovac had 290 inhabitants, 231 were Serbs and 59 were Bosniaks, and I'm referring to the local commune of Bjelovac. Is that not correct? So his answer, we would expect, would be in relation to the entire commune of Bjelovac. That's how I understand it. Yes, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: If you talk of -- I always understood Bjelovac as a commune which is comprising several villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that was the question. I read the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But wouldn't this broader or larger commune have more inhabitants than you were mentioning here? You speak of Bjelovac had 290 inhabitants. But I have in mind that Loznica and Sikiric, each of them had almost the same number of inhabitants. So how can it be that Bjelovac has only 290 inhabitants? Something just doesn't fit together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Something doesn't fit together, at least my impression.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the reference here is to a Bosnia-Herzegovina census. The ethnic breakdown in the villages and hamlets, 1992, in relation to Bratunac. All the villages that we referred to today are here. Biljaca, for example, has 655 inhabitants, just like I suggested to the witness today, 629 were Muslims and the rest Serbs. Bjelovac, 290 Serbs and 59 Muslims. Sikiric and Pobrdje are in a separate class. 257 inhabitants. Rakovac is a separate village, 355 inhabitants and 351 are Muslims. Sikiric is a separate category. Back in 1991 they had 442 inhabitants, total population 240 Muslims. 201 Serb. Voljevica, 370. That's what I have. That's the only way I can present this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: May I just express a concern? I think our trial has to be fair, not only to the accused but also to the witnesses. And can we suppose that a witness has the same perception of the composition of a commune, knowing how many people may be in this and that villages, and if these are different villages within a commune, if even the terminology of the different entities is not completely clear? So can we really assume that that is common knowledge to know on what basis a census is founded on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Perhaps I can give a hand here. Mr. Filipovic, earlier on you were told, or it was put to you and suggested to you to agree that Bjelovac had 290 inhabitants, of which about 59-something were Muslims, the rest were Serbs. And you agreed. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I suppose that's so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you agreed, what did you have in mind by Bjelovac? Was it the commune, with all the hamlets together, or was it just the village or the town of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring only to the town or village of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if you were to include the -- all the hamlets that together constitute or compose Bjelovac, now, not just the village itself but all the hamlets, what would be the population and how would it be divided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would add: Biljaca, Zaluzje, Pirici, Sikiric, Tegare, Orlica and Gornja Orlica. Those were the villages that comprised the Bjelovac local commune. The lady is setting out data from Voljevica and separating the data from Pobrdje. Pobrdje belongs to the Voljevica local commune. But the villages Loznica, not Bjelovac, the local commune, however, consists of all these villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So I think we can proceed. But basically at least we have an indication from the witness now that when he agreed that Bjelovac had 290 distributed so-and-so, he was referring to the Bjelovac, the town itself and not the local commune of Bjelovac. All right? If you have any further questions, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Although we had heard earlier on that Bjelovac is not -- is only a community or commune, but not a town as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. It's a local commune which includes also a village called Bjelovac. That's how I understand it. Now, if I am not on the right track, please tell me. I mean, I haven't been to the area. I haven't studied the demographic set-up of the area, so I don't know. I take it - correct me if I'm wrong - that you could speak of Bjelovac in two terms, in two contexts: Bjelovac as the local commune of Bjelovac, which consists of all the hamlets that Witness Filipovic mentioned a few minutes ago, and that together with the village of Bjelovac itself would constitute the local commune of Bjelovac; and then you can speak of Bjelovac as the village of Bjelovac, which had only a population of about 290, of which only about 59 were Muslims. Mr. Filipovic, I suppose you have followed what I have just stated. Am I right or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Filipovic. I will now ask you the following: Mr. Filipovic, it's correct that the SDS organised the ethnic cleansing of the entire area of several thousand Muslims, including the villages of Voljevica, Zaluzje, Biljaca, and Sikiric, in April and May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that. You've had representatives of the SDS here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, when you say "you had representatives of the SDS here," who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic, and now you're asking me things I know nothing about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you as a citizen: It's true that several thousand Muslims were brutally expelled from their homes, forced to flee into the surrounding woods and more distant and relatively safer Muslim villages; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct that they all passed through Bjelovac. Nobody touched anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not saying -- I'm not talking of Bjelovac, sir, at this point. Please respond to the questions I put to you. During this expulsion, many of them were mistreated, brutally murdered, and locked up in camps in local Serb villages, and you are aware of this, are you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, he hasn't accepted as yet that there was an expulsion, so you can't put it to him that there was an expulsion, or assume that there --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, I said it's correct that several thousand Muslims were brutally expelled from their homes, forced to flee into the woods and to relatively safer Muslim villages; is this correct? And he replied: "Yes, this is correct." It's correct that they all passed through Bjelovac. Nobody touched anyone." I understood the witness to say that they were expelled but that nobody in Bjelovac --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Obviously the witness was not agreeing with you when he said it's correct. He's telling you what is correct. It's not what you were suggesting to him but what he was suggesting to you. Yes, Mr. Filipovic. I will give you the floor, Ms. Richardson, for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, they passed through Bjelovac for a month, retreating toward Muslim villages. That's the correction I want to make. They were going where it was safer for them to shoot from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now put on the ELMO document number 00835779 of the Bratunac Crisis Staff, dated the 19th of April, 1992. It's a decision of the disarming of citizens who own weapons in the area of Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please show the B/C/S version to the witness. I don't know if he has it before him. Witness, please focus on items 1 and 2. 1: "On the territory of Bratunac municipality, the Bratunac public security station and the Territorial Defence of Bratunac municipality are authorised to disarm citizens who possess weapons in order to establish the safety and security of the citizens of Bratunac municipality." And 2: "The weapons shall be handed over to authorised officials of the Bratunac public security station and the Bratunac municipality Territorial Defence." My question is the following: Bjelovac and the villages you indicated on the map belonged to Bratunac municipality; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Miroslav Deronjic. He was the president of the Bratunac SDS, was he not, and of the Bratunac Crisis Staff, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, it's correct that in this area, only Muslims were disarmed, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not disarm them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, I didn't say you disarmed them. We'll talk about you later. I asked you if it was correct that only Muslims were disarmed during April and May 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that this document be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And this document which is being tendered and received in evidence as a Defence exhibit is being assigned the number D104.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, are you aware of the fact that the Muslim people of Voljevica, Zaluzje, and Bileca were ordered to hand over their weapons on the 20th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that they did hand over their weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in spite of the fact that they handed over their weapons, they were attacked and some of them were killed while they were being transported on the 13th of May, 1992? Did you hear that any people were killed on the 13th of May, 1992? I'm referring to a large number of people. Because you lived in the area.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what number of people. I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that anyone was killed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you weren't telling the truth when you said that violence in your area started on the 28th of June, 1992 with the attack on your village, were you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 28th of June?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was speaking about the attack on my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the violence in the area you lived in that I have just referred to started considerably before the 28th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war started, of course, started before, at Bratunac, Zvornik, and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, I'm asking you about the area you lived in, about the area you lived in.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that people left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which people, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those Muslim villagers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they left just like that, for no reason?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a war on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Filipovic, you were born in Sikiric, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't? Were you born in Sikiric?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But you know Sikiric well, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Filipovic, you told the Court, if I understood you correctly, that you lived -- or rather, that in April and May 1992, you were living in Loznica and you even marked the position of the house on the map.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was your father's house, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you personally had a house in Bjelovac, and that's where you lived just before the outbreak of the war, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you a very simple question: Did you have a house of your own in Bjelovac, and did you live there before the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, isn't it, that there were Muslim houses in the immediate vicinity of your house?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, the houses of the Sinanovic family; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The house of Rifet Dautbasic, two houses of the Efendic family, four houses of the Alic family and so on; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact number of houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to families.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Houses in Donji Bjelovac, those were also Muslim houses, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Donji Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these Muslims were looted, their houses were looted, they were intimidated, they were brutally expelled between the 11th of May and the end of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know personally that a Serb took a Muslim family to the Loznicka River because they asked him for a lift. They asked to go, and they went to Loznicka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, I'll ask you about that, but the truth is quite different. The truth is that you personally took part in these expulsions, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In late March 1992, you were already wearing a uniform and walking around Bjelovac carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you walking around Bjelovac carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At home?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you walking around Bjelovac with weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that one evening, wearing a uniform - that was in early April 1992 - you came to the door of Muriz Sinanovic with another uniformed person and demanded that he hand over to the Serbian Territorial Defence a truck that he owned? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true that he refused this, isn't it, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also true that after this, the Serbian Territorial Defence, together with soldiers from Zvornik, burst into his house, searched it, and ransacked the house and wrecked it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He then managed to escape death?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how he managed to do that if they burst into his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll come to that, Mr. Filipovic. Let's take it step by step. Right after his family was expelled, you personally usurped their property, their house; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, when you made your statement to the Prosecutor in 2000, that you own a cafe in Bjelovac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's correct, isn't it, that Muriz Sinanovic's family had a new house which was still under construction which you simply usurped and that's where you made your coffee bar; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are trying to say that this coffee bar was not in their house?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can prove this with documents. Not in the house. They had a building near the school, and I have a document from Bratunac municipality allowing me to use this prefabricated building on this location. It was not a proper house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that this was not the family house of the property of the family of Muriz Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a foundation, but I received permission to use it for a year, and it's a wooden prefabricated building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. It's true that only under the pressure of the international community for the return of the Muslims in that area you only recently left the Sinanovic family property, wrecking everything that you could?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only removed my own prefabricated building from the foundations of their house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you something else now. It is also true that in early May --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just finish this question, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a very brief question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also true that in early May 1992, in front of a number of witnesses who were shopping, you stormed the pharmacy at Bjelovac, a state-owned pharmacy, with a group of uniformed and armed people from Bjelovac; you took from Jahic Mujo, a Muslim from Bjelovac, the keys to the pharmacy, you chased him away from the pharmacy, in front of witnesses, telling him that he would no longer be selling flour to Muslims and that Muslims would no longer be able to get their supplies there because it was a Serb place; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. That's not how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how was it, then?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goods were being distributed there. There were Serbs there and Muslims too. I said: Mujo, don't give these things out, because these are socially owned. How can you distribute things that were socially owned?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. How much longer do you think you require?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At least an hour, Your Honour. I have some short video clips to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not stopping you, of course. Let's go on. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, it is true, isn't it, that after the war, you continued to harass Muslims and prevent them from returning to their homes in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the year 2000, you attacked and injured a Muslim person named Samir Jahic, who had returned to Bjelovac. You had placed a knife under his throat, forcing him to get into your vehicle, after which you took him to the Serbian police station and handed him over to the Serb police officers; that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, they helped him and they decided to press charges against you, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The result was your conviction by the first-instance court in Srebrenica, and the number of the conviction is -- the document is K322/01?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date is the 15th of February, 2002, isn't it? You were convicted for the crime of depriving a person of liberty, pursuant to Article 145, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Code of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you were sentenced to a month of imprisonment, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you something else now, Mr. Filipovic. Is it true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic. Yes, Mr. Filipovic. What do you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must dwell on this question, in order to clarify for Madam Vidovic whether it was intimidation and harassment or if maybe my emotions were being affected. She knows full well what happened. This Muslim told stories around the village about my wife being raped while she was in captivity in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't interrupt him. Have you finished? Have you finished, Mr. Filipovic, or do you want to add anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have finished. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I have Madam Usher's assistance now, please. I would like to put on the ELMO a sentence of the district court in Bijeljina, pursuant to Mr. Filipovic's appeal, in which he stated exactly what he has now told you, and we do have an English copy of this. A ruling of the district court in Bijeljina dated the 26th of September, 2003, declaring Slavoljub Filipovic's appeal as null and void and unfounded, and confirming, upholding the sentence of the first-instance court in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. The witness has already admitted that he had been arrested and convicted. I don't see the purpose of entering this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he didn't tell us that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he didn't tell us that there was an appeal and that on appeal his appeal was rejected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's fine, and that could be testimonial. I don't see the purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's leave it, because he's given an explanation for his conduct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be D105; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I was not about to use this exhibit, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you don't want to use it --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means. I do wish to use it. What I'm trying to say is that I wouldn't have used it had the witness not continued to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to draw attention to the raised hand of Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Filipovic, tell me. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have documents to prove what I'm saying. When she told me a while ago that I stole the property of the Sinanovic family and that I left the foundations under the pressure of the international forces. There are documents to show all of this, but she apparently doesn't have any documents to show what she is putting to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the time being, we are not discussing that. We are discussing this, if we are still discussing it. Yes, Madam Vidovic. Could we move to the next --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours -- yes, I can move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, is it not true that the Muslims of Voljevica, Zaluzje, Biljaca, and Sikiric who were either expelled or left the area, as you say, kept trying to return to their homes throughout June and on to December 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you not know that there was a massive body count, Muslims being killed by mines in the area, placed by the Sikiric unit and other Serb units, or killed in ambushes organised by the local Serb population?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement of 2000, you said that you had heard sounds of shooting every day and every evening, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that the shooting came from these ambushes?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, yesterday you were not telling the truth when you told us that the defence of the village was not well organised, were you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because we will go through this again. When you say "no," answer no, it means that you are admitting that you did not tell us the truth yesterday, or that you are simply rejecting Madam Vidovic's suggestion that you were not telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm rejecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But I wanted --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was my understanding too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally were in fact a soldier and you received a salary from the beginning of the war onwards; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were sending money. There was money. That's true. But who sent the money and when exactly, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Filipovic, I'll ask you this in order not to waste time. Is it not true that you were receiving a salary throughout the months of May, June, July, August, September, and October 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were receiving a salary from the Bjelovac TO, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were things like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony, you referred to Slavko Rankic, commander of the 2nd Platoon of the Bjelovac TO. Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony, you said Slavko Rankic, who in 1992 was aged about 40, was in charge of the guards; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
