utterances.text: Yes. The village security. That's what he was in charge of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, do you not agree that only the unit in which you were involved -- that that unit alone had about 160 soldiers? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about around 100 soldiers, don't we, more or less?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an exact figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I would oppose counsel using the word "soldiers." I don't think the witness has ever agreed there were soldiers. In fact, he said it was the village security, and I think it's unfair to the witness to keep using that word and have him agree to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You are perfectly right, Ms. Richardson. Could you rephrase your question, Madam Vidovic. You referred to these people as guards, or he referred to them as guards, and all of a sudden they became soldiers. There's nothing to -- maybe your contention, but he never admitted that they were soldiers. So you need to put the question first to him whether they were guards or whether they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe the interpretation was soldiers. I said fighters, for that very reason. Be that as it may, I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's cut it short, and you rephrase the question. I think the witness has followed the debate, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the units with which you were involved, how many men did it have, what you have referred to as village guards?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 100.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you. In addition to your unit, the Bjelovac TO, is it not true that in Bjelovac and around Bjelovac there were in fact other units fighting in the summer and autumn of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were providing security for the water treatment plant in Bratunac. That's why they were there. They were providing security for the water treatment plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Kunjerac and Voljevica at that time, there were Red Beret units and other volunteer units from Serbia and the Croatian Krajina that were stationed there, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They kept sending them over from Bratunac, but I don't know where they had come from originally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it not true that these units were attacking the Muslim population in the summer and autumn of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have Madam Usher's assistance now? I would like to show a document on the ELMO. This is a Bratunac Brigade document from the Bratunac Brigade set of documents, military post 7042 Bratunac. The number is 01321088 and the title is "Record of soldiers -- of a soldier's death."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, can you please look at that document. Next to the name Zarko Komenski [phoen], there is the word "volunteer." He was killed on the 14th of August, 1992 at Voljevica, in combat, in action. Novi Sad is a town in Serbia, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain the presence of Zarko Komenski from Novi Sad -- rather, what he was doing in the Muslim town of Voljevica on the 14th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The witness said: "Yes, I can." And can I please ask that the OTP do not --

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never accepted Bosnia-Herzegovina. Even now we still don't accept it. The Serbs have not yet accepted Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Serbs did not create the Republic of Srpska. It created itself. We were under the oath to preserve the brotherhood and unity of Yugoslavia, but that was gone, and that's why we didn't ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's from Novi Sad. He could have walked all the way, for all I know. Many people arrived in Zenica by plane and they survived and there were other detachments there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is not my question, is it? The truth of the matter is that at Voljevica, which is the general area of Bjelovac, there were many volunteers from Serbia fighting there, weren't there, and you know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just said a minute ago that many people could have walked there.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm just saying he may as well have walked over. But the Mujahedin arrived in Zenica by plane. The volunteers returned to Serbia and the Republika Srpska while the Mujahedin remained in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will try to ask you a question that is relevant to the case in hand. Those people, the volunteers and the Red Berets who were stationed at Kunjerac and Voljevica were in fact attacking the Muslim population that during the summer and autumn of 1992 were trying to return to their villages to get food; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that this be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be Defence Exhibit D106. Do you still require the floor, Ms. Richardson, or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I can we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I have been -- we have been put in the same category as the accused. We are now receiving interpretation in French. Yes, but this must have moved. Okay. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is true, isn't it, Mr. Filipovic, that the Bjelovac TO was not the only military unit, even in Bjelovac, fighting in the summer and autumn of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were other units who came to provide security for the water treatment plant, but they had nothing to do with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is it not correct that established and fighting in the area at the time there was also an armoured mechanised unit under the command of Radoje Radojevic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came over from time to time. As for the 14th, I don't know exactly how many of them were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that all these units took part in the fighting on the 14th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not able to see for myself. I know up to the middle of the village, but the part of the village where I was, they took no part. Because had they taken part, it wouldn't have turned out like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that a unit from Bjelovac joined the Bratunac Brigade, but only after the fall of Bjelovac. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask the usher now to put on the ELMO an excerpt from the document -- or rather, a document of the Bratunac Brigade, number 0658482 to 00658505 in B/C/S. This is a document about the establishment of the Bratunac Brigade and its area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please look at page 1 and 2. Page 1 contains the title and page 2 refers to changes in the area of responsibility. Please look at the text right underneath the heading "Changes in the area of responsibility." I quote: "On the 14th of November, 1992, by an order of the command of the Drina Corps on the formation of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, on the 14th of November, 1992, the area of responsibility of the brigade was designated in the Bratunac and Srebrenica area." There follows a description of the zone of responsibility. And then it says: "On the 14th of November, 1992, the brigade took up positions in the area -- it took control of the area." And then please look where it says: "In the area of the Sase and zinc mine, the brigade took control and defended the area." And there follows a list of toponyms and trig points. And then please look at the next passage in the area of the river Loznica, the brigade took control of the following area: The river Drina, Bjelovac, Kunjerac waterworks, 409 Loznica, Lipak trig point 488, and Sikiric. Mr. Filipovic, from this document, it appears that Bjelovac was covered by the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade a month before the attack; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was established on the 14th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But as to whether it was covered, no. All this was not covered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that this document is incorrect or what?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose you want to tender this an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Also --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that the document be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It will be assigned document Defence Exhibit number D107, but we would like a statement from you as to what this document is, where it comes from, what it is part of. I know, because we have I think seen it before, or we have seen parts of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was disclosed to the Defence by the Office of the Prosecutor on the CD Bratunac 3 collection, and I will tell you the ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I want to know is not who disclosed it to you, where you got it from. This seems to be a chapter of some bigger or longer document. What is the longer document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a document of the Bratunac Brigade, on the history of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Is it a published document? What is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document, as we received it, Your Honour, I have to say, was confiscated by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't want to hear this, and I have already told you that you should not, in the presence of the witness, give details on the provenance of the document. What I'm asking you is: This seems to be a chapter or a part of a chapter of a book, and we have seen the rest of the book or parts from the book. But you must state, confirm to us whether this is so or not. You had even the frontispiece, the first page of this book. This is what we would like you to state now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document entitled "The history of the Bratunac Brigade," and it originates from the Bratunac collection. Its ERN number, 0065842 to 00658505. I really don't know whether this document was published. I do know in what manner we received it. But I cannot say whether it was published or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Was it a diary? Was it a book? Was it a pamphlet? What was it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was compiled by the Bratunac Brigade as part of its history.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does it have an author or --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The author is the Bratunac Brigade. That's all it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you received ammunition and all other logistical support from the command centre of the brigade in Bratunac; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have ammunition, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I bought it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hate to interrupt counsel, but could we have a period in time that we're -- that Madam Vidovic is asking the witness? Because yesterday he testified that it was only after the fall that he joined the Bratunac Brigade. So if possible, we could have a period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think you're right. Yes, Madam Vidovic. When you're asking the witness whether he -- or whether they received ammunition and all other logistical support from the command centre of the brigade in Bratunac, which period of time are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll put the question as follows:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you obtain ammunition during the summer and autumn of 1992, and finally in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you answer that question, please, Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know from whom it came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then there was another question, and that was whether you had ammunition. Did you have ammunition? And if you did, when did you have ammunition? Which period of time? And are you understanding "you" as being just you, or you as a member of a group which all together become "you"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You personally. Did you have ammunition? And if so, you already told us that you did. When did you acquire it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had bought hunting ammunition earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Earlier. What do you mean by "earlier"? Earlier than when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Does that satisfy your question? Let's proceed, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will proceed. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, on the 14th of December, 1992, in Bjelovac and Sikiric, as well as in the area of Voljevica and Zaluzje, there was fierce fighting, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about Sikiric and Bjelovac. I don't know about Voljevica. How can I know what kind of fighting was there in Voljevica when I wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then tell us about Bjelovac and Sikiric? Was there fierce fighting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a fierce attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any kind of response from the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had to defend ourselves, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the response?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were firing from their houses. They had to defend themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was there just firing from houses or were there any other far more dangerous weapons used?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not where I was. We were cut off. Half of the village was cut off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, in your statement, you said that on the 14th of December, the Serbian army from Bratunac came to help the local defence.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it started getting dark, I saw them come. They came from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. This was in fact a fierce counter-attack by the Serbian forces in the entire area of Bjelovac, Sikiric, and further afield, and it took place on the same day, the 14th of December, and went on until the 17th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no counter-attack in the evening. There was an assault and then the fighting continued on the next day. But I wasn't there any longer, so I can't talk about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's true you were there on the 14th of December, 1992, in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, is it correct that during the counter-attack on Bjelovac, all possible artillery weapons were used and especially the air force?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- my objection is that again the word "counter-attack" is not something that the witness has agreed to, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. He has rejected it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Madam Vidovic still talks about it. So let's proceed. It's not going to change anything, Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct: You said that on the 14th of December, 1992, you were in Bjelovac, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that on that day, the Serb army attacked Bjelovac, Jovanovici, Sikiric, and Loznicka Rijeka from the air, with the intention of driving out the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian army attacking Bjelovac and Sikiric? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now ask that the video recording of the attack on Bjelovac be played. This is video 3901, entitled "Video on the attack on Bjelovac, Bratunac," disclosed by the Prosecution, and on the original video it begins with minute 33, and the Defence has not edited this video in any way. The time shown is the time on the original recording, except that we added a translation. If there is any objection to the translation, I think it is absolutely correct, but if there is an objection, I ask that it be taken as a draft translation and it can be checked afterwards. This is the video as we received it. Could you please play video number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we'll need to approach it as we did yesterday, of course with the caveat that the translation itself is not testimony of the truth of the contents of what it says, anyway, contents of the ... Yeah. And again, Madam Vidovic, please don't state where this document came from, where you obtained it from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the sound be played also?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're asking me? I will have to go back to the technicians, who are on my right. Wait, Madam Vidovic. Usually they solve the problem. They are very capable, very capable people.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone was not switched on, so the interpreter didn't catch what the counsel said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you need to repeat what you said, because your microphone was switched off and the interpreters couldn't follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we checked this with the technicians beforehand, and it was in good order. It's very important for us that this video be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It will be shown. Don't worry. It's not the end of the world. These things happen. I've passed through this a hundred times. And at the end of the day, at least in 99 cases, it was solved.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you have seen the footage, haven't you? Do you recognise the area? Don't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear the comment being made? Did you see the planes firing, how well they were targeting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you understand what sort of an attack this was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you assume that we should have just lain down and died, that we should have all been killed, I expect.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please, I don't think it's appropriate for the witness to be making these comments. Please answer my question, because my question was entirely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Filipovic, I have to draw your attention at this juncture that you have no right to reply to Madam Vidovic when she is putting questions to you in the way that you have replied. She has asked you a very legitimate question, which has been going on now for quite some time. First she asked you whether you recall that on that day, the Serbian air force, or the army, through the Serbian plane, did intervene in the conflict, and you said no. And in fact, you showed that you were absolutely surprised, even at this being suggested to you. Now you have been shown a film in which it is being suggested to you that you should have been able to see aircraft, military aircraft, taking apart -- taking part in an attack or whatever, and you're being asked questions in relation to what you have seen. And the first question was whether you recognise the area, and you said: "Yes, I recognise the area." The next question was in relation to the aircraft, and instead of explaining, you're just trying to counter Madam Vidovic in a way which is not legitimate and which I will not allow. So I invite you, please, to answer the question, and nothing but the question, in accordance with the oath that you took yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the question was: Is it not true that there were aircraft targeting this area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now, please, place this document on the ELMO. These are stills taken from the video. Can we please have these photographs placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at these photographs. This specific photograph shows a plane, and you can see the time: 9.26. The date is 14th of December, 1992. In relation to that, my question is the following: Is it not true that the bombardment began at 9.26, at the latest?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move that this photograph and this whole portion of the video be moved into evidence and assigned two numbers. We do have other videos to show, and it may be convenient that all these -- Your Honours, for the time being, I move that this photograph be assigned a number as a Defence exhibit. I will move on with this video. We have several minutes of it left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So this still from the video that was shown to the witness and which will be, according to the declaration just made by Madam Vidovic, tendered into evidence at a later stage, this still is being marked -- admitted and marked as Defence Exhibit D107. When you say 9.26, is it 9.26 in the morning? I mean, it's obvious that it is, but I want a declaration from you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, yes. 108, sorry. Not 107; 108. 108.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have one more question in relation to this. You heard a comment being made by a voice in this footage, saying: "You don't know who is fighting whom." Is it not true, Mr. Filipovic, that in Bjelovac, on that day, there was chaos? Both Serbs and Muslims were engaged in hand-to-hand combat; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now play the video, the video from the same spot. The original -- I'm trying to assist my colleagues from the OTP. The time is 42:10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you proceed, Ms. Vidovic, let me ask the witness a question. We've just seen some houses, very distinctly. Are you familiar with those houses? Would you recognise the place where the camera is shooting, where the filming is taking place from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Across the way from Bjelovac, at Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically what we are seeing, then, is the camera is looking in the direction of Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Madam Vidovic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it finished? But it has gone -- no. It's gone back to 10:32, 10:32, which is -- let's -- I think they will find .... All right. Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, did you hear the comments being made by these people?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A voice said: "This was not on fire until a short while ago," and another voice replied: "There was a plane that dropped about ten bombs."

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but who does he mean? It wasn't burning until a short while ago. Maybe the house caught fire. You know, when a bomb is dropped on a house, you know what it's like. It starts burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the comment being made by a male voice: "Oh, yes. Oh, yes. It's all them in the houses now." "Them" means Muslims, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure who they mean by "them."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, is it not correct that there are comments being made here to the effect that a plane hit the houses and a truck?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the house was not specified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, not specified, but a house?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They said a house. But they didn't say that it was hit by a plane.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can continue now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here houses in Loznicka Rijeka were mentioned, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, is it not true that this damage could have been caused by a plane bombing?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will continue with one piece of video.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you have seen the footage. Did you notice a voice saying: "Yes, they will be shelling it." And then there was a comment made: "Yes, they've shelled it now."

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were comments coming from the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "the other side"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the child's voice?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But the comments where to this effect, do you not remember that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question related to this portion of the footage: It was said that they were mixed. Is it not correct - let me ask you again - that there was hand-to-hand combat in the area and that everything was mixed up?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now show you two photographs from the same video. This is for the sake -- for the benefit of the Chamber and the OTP. Can you please show the witness these photographs. These photographs are stills from the same video footage. Witness, can you please look at the time, the time recorded on the tape, and look at this photograph. You can see a bomb, a plane dropping a bomb.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see the time, 15:20, can you not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we see the next photograph. The time is 15:21?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose you want to tender these in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the photo with the biplane dropping a bomb, or more than one bomb, will be Defence Exhibit D109. The document showing a house burning will be D110.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, I will put a question in connection with this. You've just seen the second photograph, on which, at 9.26, a plane is shown. Now you see the time here, 15:20. Isn't it correct that this bombing lasted all day and that you must have seen it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't go on all day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, for how long did it go on for, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because now it's already past the hour that you mentioned. How much -- I'm not stopping, you but how much more time do you require?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have a lot, Your Honour. Maybe about ten minutes or 15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You because that basically would bring us to the break, which basically means that your new witness could be here for a maximum of 45 minutes. So in the meantime, think about what your preference is, whether you want to start him off today or whether you prefer to postpone everything until Monday. It's up to you. I mean, I'm not going to interfere. I'm just trying to organise the rest of the sitting. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Think about it and let me know later. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, my initial reaction is, I understand there will be some re-examination, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I am saying. I mean, basically we're talking of past the break. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 45 minutes at the most. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, as far as the Prosecution is concerned, we're ready to go. I mean, I've got my notes ready. However, the man has been sitting here for quite some time and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Give him a coffee and decide whether he is going to stay here a little bit longer. Make sure he is made to feel comfortable. That's all. Because for these witnesses sitting in one room, a small room, for long hours, it's frustrating. It's -- MR. DI FAZIO: I know. That's my point, if Your Honours please. If we continue, then we have the break, then we have some re-examination, and then we're left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. We will have the re-examination before the break. MR. DI FAZIO: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I thought. MR. DI FAZIO: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not a problem. I don't have that many questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So basically you have 45 minutes. But since I told you earlier on, it's up to you whether you want to start him off for just 45 minutes today or not. I mean, it's up to you. But think about it and let us know when we get to the break. And if you decide that you should start on Monday with this witness, then you can in the meantime take action, send a message, get him going, and then tell us later. All right. Yes, Madam Vidovic. Sorry for having interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you, Mr. Filipovic, whether this bombing and shelling could have caused damage to people and property in Bjelovac on the 14th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, did I understand you properly yesterday when you said that you didn't have a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask for a very brief video to be played, video number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Again we have the sound problem. I am not hearing any sound.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe just one scene is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, do you agree that this is you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that on the 14th of December, 1992, you were wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, this is the 15th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Filipovic. Do you agree that on the 15th of December you were wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left my house almost naked. I just took a black leather jacket. I don't know who gave this to me. I had to put something on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Filipovic, you told us that throughout this period, you did not wear a uniform, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move on. Mr. Filipovic, it's true that your wife, children, and mother were not killed on that day, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father was killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was killed in combat, as a fighter, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the yard of his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he killed in combat?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed in the yard of his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm asking you: Was he fighting?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask the usher -- but before that, I move that the parts of the videos we have shown be assigned exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This one and the previous one are not the same video; no? They are different? This video clip that we have seen now and the previous one --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first three clips are on one videotape, and the other is on another videotape. So I ask that the first three be given one exhibit number, and the last one another exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the three video clips contained in the same tape, dealing with the attack, air attack, in the vicinity of Bjelovac is being assigned Defence Exhibit number D111. The other video we have just seen, which depicts the witness being interviewed is being assigned the Defence Exhibit number D112.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness be shown D87. This is a list of combatants of the 1st Bratunac Light Brigade, killed from the 18th of April 1992 until the 25th of September, 1995, page 00661857.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look under number 185, please. The name here is Filipovic. That's on page 1. And please look at number 185. Filipovic Milisava Dragoljub. Is that your father?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Killed on the 14th of December, 1992, in combat defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you don't know, say "I don't know," Mr. Filipovic. And if you know, tell us that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was killed in the yard, in front of the front door. If that's combat, he was -- then he was killed in defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Would you look at number 184. Is this your brother, Filipovic, Dragoljub and Dragan?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 14th of December, was he fighting? Was he a combatant, and was he killed as such?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there. Whether he managed to fight or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was he a member of that unit in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was he a member of the unit in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the village guard. He came from time to time, because he worked in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This document already has an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Filipovic, I will put a few questions to you about how your wife was taken prisoner and about your efforts to learn something about this. In your statement to the Prosecutor in the year 2000, you said that you had heard a conversation between Milos Okanovic and a person whom you say is Naser Oric. I will give you the statement, if you need it, but I will remind you now that on that occasion you said: "Milos interrupted the radio connection and said Naser, You should be ashamed of yourself. What kind of a commander are you when you're holding women and children hostage? Naser replied, Are you the person from Serbia who's catching our frequency? Naser then said, Nothing will happen to them."

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You signed that statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said something quite different. You said: "You've imprisoned" -- or rather, you said that Okanovic said: "You've imprisoned a six-month-old baby. Aren't you ashamed of yourselves?" And he replied: "Whoever is on the front line is a soldier, in my view."

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, when you were making your statement four years ago, your memory of these events was fresher, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something I will never be able to erase from my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that four years ago your memory was fresher?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that what you say now differs from what you said four years ago?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Four years ago, you said that this person Naser replied: "Nothing will happen to them."

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said he replied: "Whoever is at the front line is a soldier, in my view."

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than one thing was said. More than one thing was said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the truth, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not contradictory or mutually exclusive, Madam Vidovic. The two statements can coexist without any problems at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll put it like this:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, four years ago, you didn't say that he said: "Whoever is at the front line is a soldier, in my view." Now you were simply trying to represent Oric in a worse light; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I said is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, nothing bad happened to your wife and children when they were taken prisoner; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Why was I indicted? Why did I spend a month in prison, madam?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, I'm asking you about when your wife was taken prisoner. I'll put it like this: After your wife returned, you talked to her about the time she spent in prison, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She must have told you that she was not held in the town of Srebrenica at all but in Salocusa [phoen]; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She also told you she wasn't kept in a prison, didn't she?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She also told you that no one mistreated her, intimidated her, or did anything bad to her; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you didn't mention any of these facts, did you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let's go back to Mr. Milos Okanovic. It's true, isn't it, that he was a ham radio operator and not a member of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you went to see him because you knew that he had contacts with other ham radio operators, including Muslim ham radio operators in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd been to see him before. I knew him from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that he had contacts with other ham radio operators in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the whole territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. Yes. Thank you. Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Naser Sulejmanovic was a well-known ham radio operator from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Naser Sulejmanovic was in fact a person who sent ham radio reports from Srebrenica to the media in Sarajevo, and even to the foreign media, such as the BBC, CNN, and so on. Milos Okanovic knew this, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you something else now. In the conversation you quoted, this person called Naser certainly didn't introduce himself and say: "I am the commander of the Srebrenica forces, Naser Oric," did he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to two questions by the Prosecutor as to whether you knew or had met Mr. Oric, and whether you could recognise his voice, yesterday you replied: "I had occasion to meet Naser Oric. I repaired his car on several occasions in 1991. I was friends with his father. We exchanged business deals."

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, in your statement to the Prosecutor, you said -- let me just say that you said quite decisively that you repaired that car for him on several occasions in 1990.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was in 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In your statement, you said that you had completed the secondary civil engineering school.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're not a car mechanic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did work as one for three years, and I do have a diploma, and I did work for three years with a man who repaired cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never had a car mechanic's shop. You work in the Sase mine, and you did quite a different kind of job, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But in the afternoons I worked at home, or rather, I worked at that car mechanic's shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It's true that Mr. Oric's father was a highly qualified mechanic who repaired all types of vehicles, and you know this, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially diesel engines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, there was really no need for Mr. Oric to pay for the maintenance of his vehicle, to pay anyone else.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't pay. He would come together with his father, and we did some work for him on two or three occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, in fact, you never met Naser Oric in your life, or spoke to him, and that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Filipovic, since you say that you know Mr. Oric, that from 1998 [as interpreted] he lived and worked in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, do you know that, in actual fact --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correction in the transcript. From 1988. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, do you know that Mr. Oric spent the entire year 1990 carrying out special tasks in Kosovo and was only back in Belgrade as late as the 5th of August, 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but he did come over.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm referring here to -- he went back to Sarajevo, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't go back anywhere, but he came to Srebrenica a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then, Your Honours, I will refer to paragraph 3 of the OTP's indictment against the accused Naser Oric. I'm not sure if it's necessary to show the witness this portion. I don't think there's any need to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can put the question. Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think showing Mr. Filipovic our indictment is -- it would be helpful at all. And in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put the question to the witness. I don't think he needs to see --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I'll ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... which part of the indictment are you ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, this is paragraph 3, Naser Oric, an ex-policeman. Mr. Filipovic, it is true, isn't it, that in 1990, Oric -- I think probably the best thing for me would be to begin. It is true, isn't it, Mr. Filipovic, that in 1988, he had completed a six-month course in Zemun. He did an internship at the Savski Venac in Belgrade as a member of the police unit for special tasks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is the witness the official recorder, historian of Naser Oric? Why are you asking the witness these questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. The witness said he knew Naser Oric and that he was friends with his father. And that's why I'm asking this question: Is it not true that he spent the entire year of 1990 in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's already told you, return to Serbia --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's already answered that question and he also told you that he used to return to Srebrenica on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, in actual fact, you made up your meetings with Mr. Oric in order to find a reason why his voice was familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He gave my former boss 50 pieces of ammunition from the army on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, can I ask you this question: Did you ever listen to any voices in radio communication?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that this voice is distorted to a high degree in radio communication?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It depends on the range and the distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Filipovic. I'll move on to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is well beyond the six minutes that you said. Basically you have disrupted all that I had mentioned earlier. You are not -- but I'm -- anyway, are you understanding what I'm saying? Are you receiving interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. I will just ask another question, one more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ask as many questions as you like. I told you straight and plain before that I will not be stopping you, because this is an important witness. And you're touching on matters that are important. But you should not have given us an indication that you were going to conclude in six minutes, leading me into believing that we could conclude the re-examination and any questions that we could have here before the break and then we would have 45 minutes for the next witness. Because obviously you're not even going to finish by the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have the break and we will continue after the break. In the meantime, I think you decide what you want to do with the next witness. But if you think you're going to send him back to the hotel, I would ask that before we go for the break, we will escort this witness out, we will bring in the other witness, and I will apologise to him and explain to him what has happened. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, may I indicate this: I'll go back and I'll say to this witness -- I'll ask that they take him back to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not enough, Mr. Di Fazio. I have been brought up in another -- in a different legal cultural. We face the witness and we explain to him. But I would like first that this witness be escorted out. I don't want -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours feel that absolutely necessary, with respect to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely. Definitely. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So please, Madam Usher, you first escort this witness to wherever you're keeping him, and then we'll see him again after the break. And after having done that, please bring in the other witness and I will explain to him what is happening. Yes. Unless we decide, unless we decide to go on for a little while and finish with this witness. MR. DI FAZIO: That would be ideal. And if Your Honours please, with all respect, I can explain the situation to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know you can, Mr. Di Fazio. I appreciate it. But I don't think it's your fault, and we are responsible for the Trial Chamber and the trial, and therefore it's our responsibility to address the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: As Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At least that's how I have been -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now if you want, we can do away with the break, if we have the concurrence of everyone, provided I have the word of everyone that we will finish in ten minutes. This witness does not have any protective measures, does he? MR. DI FAZIO: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please sit down, Mr. Nikolic. Thank you. I am speaking in English, but I want a confirmation from you that what I am saying is being translated to you in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I should have said "good afternoon" to you, but it's now evening. So I say good evening to you, Mr. Nikolic, and welcome to this Tribunal. I know that you have been here in The Hague already a few days.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know that you may have been given the indication before that possibly we would have been able to start with your testimony and finish with your testimony today, enabling you then to go back home for the weekend. But unfortunately, things did not turn out as we wished them to. The previous witness has taken much longer to finish his testimony, and we haven't finished with him as yet, and the one before him also took more than what we had anticipated. These were important witnesses. We couldn't reduce the time. And you are also an important witness, and we want to make sure that you are relaxed and not frustrated and angry with us before you start your testimony. So today we still have to continue with the other witness, and we will not be able to start with your testimony. I am sorry this had to be like this. It was not our intention. It was certainly not our desire to have it this way. I apologise to you on behalf of the Trial Chamber. And I promise you that we will do our utmost to make your weekend here as relaxing and enjoyable as possible, and that on Monday, please God, we will start with your testimony and do our utmost to finish. Do you accept our apology?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for your sense of responsibility, and also for having understood, for your understanding. I'm pretty sure you understand that this is not due to the fault of anyone; it's just -- these things happen, and when they happen, they end up creating problems. So you will be escorted now by our usher and you will be taken back to the hotel and you will be looked after in the course of the weekend. And make sure that if you have any wish or any desire to make your rest here in The Hague over the weekend easy and relaxing, to tell so the officials, the persons that will be taking care of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have a nice evening, and also a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I suggest now it's not even fair any further, any more, to suggest that we proceed. I think we have a break. Or do you prefer to proceed and finish? How much more time do you think you have? Take all time you require.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think seven or eight minutes. Your Honours, my apologies. Maybe ten minutes. But I get interrupted all the time. But there's no witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Richardson, how much time do you require?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, no more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that makes it already roughly 20. You have some questions, Judge Eser. So we're talking about 20, 25 minutes. So we'll have a 15-minute break,, 15-minute break is being suggested to me. Is that agreeable to everyone, the other interpreters and the technicians?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. The technician needs 20? Yes. All right. We'll have it 20. I'm afraid I can't help more than that. So we will reconvene in 20 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, while there's a moment free, I might mention something which I was otherwise going to mention at the end of the hearing. There's an objection today from the Prosecution concerning -- here comes the witness. I'll deal with it afterwards. It need only detain us only two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll hear the submission after the witness is finished. If it's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. It was just to fill in the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Come in, and let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. One moment until he puts the earphones on. Are you receiving interpretation, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, in your testimony of yesterday, you said you had left Bjelovac and then returned to Bjelovac, and in your statement of 2000, you said about ten days after the Serbs retook Bjelovac. Yesterday, however, you said in February. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The truth is, is it not, that around Bjelovac, Sikiric, and on that entire area, while you were absent, fierce fighting was going on? Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Serbs retook this area through combat activities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Filipovic, that these combat activities could have been one of the causes of the damage to the houses in this area?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you said that you were liable for military service and that you were a conscript in the Army of Republika Srpska for about six months, from late 1993 and for a part of 1994. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the dates, but yes, I was a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when? In what period of time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in 1994?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1994, on the 14th of February, that's when I didn't want to be a member of the army anymore, but I was until then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct, isn't it? So you say that as of the 14th of February, you were no longer a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying that you were not in the army in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to put on the ELMO a document of the Bratunac Brigade, 01319944, entitled "List of advance salaries paid for February 1994 [as interpreted], military post 7042." And would you turn the page, Mr. Filipovic, please. It ends with number 958, because it's an excerpt from a document. And do you see that it says here "Bjelovac barracks"? Would you please look at number 3. It says: "Filipovic Dragoljuba Slavoljub."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your name?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look -- this is in the Bjelovac barracks - next to your name is says "VO," which means military conscript, and there is a number.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is not that the name of your military booklet?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It may be, but I don't know it by heart.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am speaking of February 1995, and the document bears the date February 1995. May this be corrected in the transcript. I wasn't referring to February 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. All throughout, I thought you were referring to February 1994, because that's what I heard before. But now that you're saying that you're referring to February 1995, I want to make sure that the witness has understood that these documents refer to February 1995 and not to February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you understood, Witness?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I told you, I wasn't sure about the date when I was a member of the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will put the question as follows: I asked you whether in 1995 you were a member of the Army of Republika Srpska. Your answer was no. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have now before you a list of advance salaries paid for February 1995, military post 7042. Please look at these columns. There's the last name, the first name, a rank, then there is a code number and the number of a military booklet.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now please look at page 2, where it says "Bjelovac barracks."

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But is this the number of your military booklet?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you were not telling the truth, then, when you said that after February 1994 you were not a member.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I kept telling you I wasn't sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you in July 1995, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can show that with documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no need to do that. Just answer my question.

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the cooperative in Bratunac. I was a tractor driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not a military conscript?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. I move that this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this will be, Gerold, number D113? This will be Defence Exhibit D113. Yes. Is there re-examination, Ms. Richardson?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if there is, could you please keep it to the bare minimum. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Re-examined by Ms. Richardson:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, you were shown videos of planes flying overhead, and could you tell us where -- if you recall those videos, the area that the planes were flying over. Could you tell us: Was this the wider area of Bjelovac or was -- or could you tell whether it was specifically over your village -- over your hamlet, I think Loznica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was around Bjelovac. About Loznica, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the attack started at 5.30 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the attack started and you ran outside, were you able to see any planes flying overhead?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The planes arrived much later, at about 10.00, or maybe 9.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you hear the planes or were you able to see them from where you were?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from my house. Not from the shelter. I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So how do you know that there were planes flying over around 10.00 or 9.30? Was that from the photographs you were shown or --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry. That's not a fair question at all. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree. Yes. Just restrict your question to the first part of it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How can you tell that the planes arrived at 9.30 or 10.00, Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the video. That day seemed very short to me, as short as an hour. I'm unable to orient myself in time with respect to that day, but I saw this on the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I note that the witness was prompted to give that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but he said it. He's given that answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I certainly take offence to what counsel just tried to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you -- when you were hiding in -- I believe you mentioned there were two homes that you were hiding in during the attack. Were you able to hear planes flying over or planes dropping bombs?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could only hear them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, those planes -- what time did you -- were you able to see soldiers on the ground during the period --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. This raises an issue which I was going to raise earlier. We realise -- first of all, the Prosecution objected to us using the word "soldiers." It's clear now that there may be a big interpretation problem between soldiers, "vojnici"; fighters, "borci." It may be this has run right through the whole trial to date. But that's why we object to questions saying whether it's civilians or soldiers. The Prosecution should always only ask the question: Who did you see? What were they wearing. And it's for Your Honours to decide whether they were soldiers or not. They may be persons with some uniform, they may be fighters. Soldiers implies being members of an army, which is a value judgement, in our submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I respond. My question is in direct response to what the Defence stated, that there was hand-to-hand combat on the ground between two sides and that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that has been denied, has been rejected by the --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just seeking to clarify that he was not able to see Serb soldiers from where he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you see any persons fighting in any case, irrespective of whether they were wearing uniform or not? Mr. Filipovic, look at me, please. You have told us that you saw Serb villagers shooting from their houses. That you have told us already. Apart from that -- apart from that, in the surroundings of your village, could you see anyone engaged in fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And who did you see, or what did you see? Who was fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people were in the shelters. You could see them raise their heads from the shelter, fire, and then duck again. And people were killed around their houses. Then they took shelter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And they were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then the fighting wasn't as fierce any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And they were fighting and they were shooting against whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were shooting at the attackers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And who were the attackers, apart from the fact that you have already told us that they were Muslims? Who were they? Were they civilians? Were they wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only saw one of them with a uniform on with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Apart from these Muslim attackers, did you see any other persons who would not be Muslims who were engaged in direct fighting with those Muslims attackers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move from there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you stated, Mr. Filipovic, testified that the attack lasted all day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was the first time you saw Serb soldiers that day?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just before dark, when I set out towards Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't see them at 5.30 in the morning, and you didn't see them as you were making your way to the various houses?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified on direct that you had been mobilised in 1992; correct?
