utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received call-up notes. Whether it was in April or May, but we remained at home. We didn't go anywhere. We didn't respond to those call-up notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you simply continued to be a member of the village guard, in your mind, and not a soldier serving with the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were shown Exhibit -- Defence Exhibit 101. You were shown a number of exhibits. Let me just take you back to a particular one where the document shown to you was from the 1st Platoon, and Defence asked if you knew someone by the name of Milovanovic Stojadin. Was that the name of the person? Do you recall? Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has already told us that he knows him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just -- I'm getting there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to what you were shown, indicating that this person was a member of the 1st Platoon and that he had received an automatic weapon in Belgrade -- sorry, that he works in Belgrade, but he had received an automatic weapon, do you know anything personally about that? Did you see him with this weapon?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your name was not on this list that was shown to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type weapon did you have?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a hunting rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to -- and this is my final question, Your Honour - with respect to your wife and children, Defence asked if anything bad had happened to them. In your mind, did you consider the fact that they had been --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry. I can tell already this is going to be an extremely leading question. The Prosecution sometimes thinks that re-examination is for leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't heard the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: She is about to make a suggestion of what might have been in his mind. Why doesn't she simply ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. Let her make the question, and if it's not a fair question I will stop her.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: She'll say: Did you consider the fact that they had been detained, bad treatment, or something of that nature. Well, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I inquire?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question. In the interests of time, I was trying to sum up, give a much broader question than I intended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife and children were taken prisoner following the attack or during the attack in Bjelovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, they were taken prisoner by the Bosnian Muslim army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry. I really object to these questions. Taken prisoner, first of all, isn't something within his knowledge. It implies all sorts of things. One could say that they had been evacuated for their safety. And these are loaded terms which are being used. But secondly, the Bosnian Muslim army, the witness has said that he saw one person in uniform that day. And so now she is asking this witness to assert that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What did he see, what did he hear, that's what we're interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please rephrase your question, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, what happened to your wife and children on December 14, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did they remain in Bjelovac or -- where they resided or did they disappear from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They disappeared from there, and my mother together with them, not only my children and my wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who took them?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He hadn't even seen it. We've covered this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He hasn't said that they were taken. How come they disappeared? Do you have an explanation for their disappearance? Mr. Filipovic, do you have an explanation for their disappearance? Did they leave the town of their own free will or not? How come that you no longer found them in Bjelovac? They disappeared from Bjelovac? What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were taken away. They were imprisoned, captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you see that happening or did you assume or come to that conclusion, without seeing anyone doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see them being taken away. What I thought at the time is that they were burnt alive in the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And later on they were exchanged; no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who was the exchange made with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No one informed me about the exchange. I didn't know. I drove the water tanker from Dubovija [phoen]. I was sitting in a cafe in Bratunac and then a man came over and said: "They brought your mother, wife and children there. Momir Nikolic." They were exchanged at Skelani. So Momir Nikolic was the one. I don't know where they were exchanged from or why. That's what they know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But who brought them over? I mean, who surrendered them back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Momir Nikolic is a Serb, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He wasn't keeping them himself, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He was in charge of the exchange at Skelani, with the Muslim forces. He was the chief of security of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I mean, I should have become a dentist, not a judge, because you have to extract. Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic, did your wife tell you that she was exchanged?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And thank you, Ms. Richardson. Judge Brydensholt. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: When you saw the video, where you were wearing something which seems to be a uniform, you told that that was something you have got between the 14th and the 15th of December. That was how I understood it. Could you explain a bit more about what kind of uniform did you get, and where did you get it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asleep when the attack began. I left my house with no socks on or boots or any clothes, for that matter. The house where I spent the entire day, I found a black jacket there and then I crossed over into Serbia wearing the black jacket. I gave it to someone in Bratunac. It was in December. But I see there was an olive-drab jacket, which is part of a uniform that I wore at the time. I saw it in the footage. You can see the white shirt underneath. You can see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Then I have another question. I understand that your house was under construction, the new house, at the bank of the Drina River. That house was a bit south of Bjelovac itself. You said at some time, at a given time, that you were cut off. What do you mean with that? Was it only your part of the village which was attacked, and was the other part of Bjelovac still defended when you left?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably the house that was on fire was being defended. The photograph that madam showed that was wrong, that's my house. And up to that point, everything had been killed and there was resistance down towards Bratunac. They didn't catch us there. There were only 150 metres to go to the Drina River, and they approached us from the back. Between 50 and 150 from Sikiric, they didn't even have a hundred metres. Just next to the road by the roadside. That's where they were waiting. And they approached us from the back. As far as the other half of Bjelovac, I have no idea, because as far as I know, no people were killed in the other half of Bjelovac. We -- this side of the middle of town, we were the ones who were killed, in this house that was on fire. It's a family home belonging to me, and there was a ground floor that was totally new. A house was being built at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Some of the questions which I had have already been answered or asked and answered. I would a question with regard to the videos, before I ask my question, put my question to the witness. I would like to ask the Defence counsels: Is it known who had taken the videos which have been shown here?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I think -- I think it will not be proper to have this information given in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will provide this information as soon as the witness leaves the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I would just ask the witness: Did you -- had you seen the videos before? The videos which we saw here, had they been new to you or have you seen them before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You saw them before. So you have been aware that these videos exist?

utterances.speaker: SLAVOLJUB FILIPOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That basically brings us to the end of your testimony, Mr. Filipovic, which lasted more than we had anticipated. On behalf of the Trial Chamber, and that's on my behalf and on behalf of Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser, I would like to thank you for having accepted to come over and give evidence, testimony, in this case against Naser Oric. You will now be attended to this court, out of the courtroom by Madam Usher, and you will receive all the assistance you require to return to your home. Before you leave this courtroom, may I wish you a safe journey back home, on behalf of everyone here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll deal with these two matters. First, the person, the name of the person or persons who shot the videos. We saw two. So I don't know if we're talking of the same one. Probably not. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the way it's explained on the list that was forwarded to us when -- in connection with the testimony of Ms. Racine Manas, we're about to hear her, she'll appear as a witness, the note was that Witness Filipovic was the one who handed over this video footage. That is also a conclusion based on his own testimony. On his statement in 2000, he mentions that he handed over two videos to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It doesn't explain who shot -- who made the videos.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And the explanation as to who, the video was taken by a person from Serbia. The video, the way the witness has explained in his statement, the video shows Bjelovac. It shows houses ablaze. Milos Okanovic, a person that he referred to, which means shot the video from his terrace at Grabovica. And that's what he said in his testimony, or at least that's what I understood him to be saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Is it known who the persons have been who -- the voices which we heard are known?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the voices belongs to Milos Okanovic. That much is certain. He is commenting on the footage as he's taking the footage. And this is the person referred to by the witness, by Mr. Filipovic, today and yesterday. That's as much as I know, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Jones, did you still want to raise the other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I would, Your Honour, very briefly. But I do think it's a terribly important issue. It's firstly a linguistic issue, which is that we've heard that -- the term soldiers "vojnici," has been at least on one occasion perhaps mistranslated and "borci" which refers to fighters. For that reason, and because, as I said, the term "soldiers" implies perhaps being a member of an army, it's a matter which I've considered objecting to on occasions when the question has been put to witnesses: Were these soldiers or civilians. Because it's far more complex than that. And I mention the matter now firstly, as I say, as a linguistic issue. Even the witness himself is careful to refer to attackers today, "napadaci." I mention it because it may be a problem running through the transcripts to date, that there might be that translation problem. But also to, in a sense, give notice for future objections that we do object to the Prosecution saying: Were these civilians or soldiers? It oversimplifies matters. They should say: Who did you see, what were they wearing? And that way by carefully seeing what the witness saw, we can -- Your Honours can reach a conclusion whether they're soldiers or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Point taken. Point taken. And we will regulate accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, point taken with respect to what Mr. Jones just mentioned. But I should also add and request the same from the Defence, if a witness is testifying to a village guard and it's been re-characterised as "fighter," I think it's just as bad as saying the word "soldier." So I think both sides should be very careful of whatever they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll regulate the matter. Now that we know of your concerns, we will regulate the matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If it's the VRS, obviously we need to suggest that people were members of the VRS. That's a different matter, obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it that there is -- Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would also like to say the following: When we speak about documents which read fighters of the Bratunac Brigade, fighters of the 1st Platoon, fighters, I really can't say, fighters are members of the TO, Territorial Defence, for example, I can't say "the TO guard" or anything like that. If I'm to interpret the document at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I said -- I don't think this calls for an exchange of -- we will use all the flexibility that there is available and we will regulate the matter accordingly. I mean, if there is a serious objection at any given point, we will give it due consideration and we will decide whether it's fit and proper to use the noun "soldier" or "soldiers" or whether it's more proper to use some other word. We'll play it by the ear, according to the different circumstances that we will be dealing with. So we will adjourn now until Monday. Monday we are meeting in the morning, we are sitting in the morning. I don't recall which courtroom. I just want to wish you all a nice weekend. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 6th day of December, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
